# Known bugs of graph queries that BigQuery's answers to unverified cases found, with the graph
# fixture of setup.sql. Each case gives BigQuery's answer after `!>`, which the emulator does not
# give yet; see ../known_bugs.txt.

# Observed BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers. graph-patterns.md calls a NULL, zero,
# negative, infinite or NaN cost under ANY CHEAPEST a runtime error, and GoogleSQL's reference
# implementation fails when a path's total cost overflows its type. BigQuery raises these errors
# where the result depends on the selected path (graph_cheapest.txt), but counted these paths,
# whose number does not, without an error.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-patterns.md
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount > 0, NULL, e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "4"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount - 100]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "4"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST -e.amount]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "4"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IEEE_DIVIDE(e.amount, 0)]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "4"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0) + e.amount]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "4"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e1:Transfers COST 9223372036854775807]->(b:Account)-[e2:Transfers COST 9223372036854775807]->(c:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
!> "5"

# BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers. Contrary to the description of nested
# STRUCTs in third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-sql-queries.md, BigQuery
# rejects returning a joined ROW. It allows projecting scalar fields underneath it: when the
# edge is not inlined, P is nested under SP. SP survives a NULL or unmatched destination key.
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(
  SELECT AS STRUCT id, SP.edge_size, SP.P.id AS place_id, SP.P.name AS place_name
  FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlaces', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
))
!> "[{\"id\":1,\"edge_size\":3,\"place_id\":1,\"place_name\":\"p\"},{\"id\":2,\"edge_size\":4,\"place_id\":2,\"place_name\":null},{\"id\":3,\"edge_size\":5,\"place_id\":null,\"place_name\":null},{\"id\":4,\"edge_size\":6,\"place_id\":null,\"place_name\":null}]"
SELECT * FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlaces', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
!> error contains: Returning expressions of type ROW is not allowed
SELECT * FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
!> error contains: Returning expressions of type ROW is not allowed
SELECT id, P.id AS place_id, P.name AS place_name FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
!> error contains: Unrecognized name: P
SELECT id, TYPEOF(P) AS place_type FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
!> error contains: Unrecognized name: P
